programs.title_tr: Pratt & Whitney GTF (PW1100G) Toz Metal Kusuru & Yere İndirmeler
programs.title_en: Pratt & Whitney GTF (PW1100G) Powder Metal Defect & Groundings
programs.current_status_tr: Yüksek basınçlı türbin disklerindeki mikroskobik toz metal kirliliği nedeniyle küresel çapta yüzlerce A320neo/A321neo uçağı planlanmamış motor bakımına alındı. Ortalama motor revizyon süresi (TAT) 250-300 günü buluyor.
programs.current_status_en: Contaminated powder metal in high-pressure turbine disks required accelerated inspections; hundreds of A320neo family jets grounded globally with MRO shop turnaround times reaching 250-300 days.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: THY filosundaki yaklaşık 30-40 adet A320/A321neo uçağı yerde bekliyor; kapasite açığını kapatmak için ıslak kiralama (wet lease) ve mevcut A320ceo uçaklarının hizmet ömrünü uzatma yoluna gidildi. Pegasus filosu ağırlıklı CFM LEAP motorlu olduğu için doğrudan etkilenmedi.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Turkish Airlines has 30-40 A321neo aircraft parked; capacity shortfall managed via wet leases and extending older A320ceo service lives. Pegasus remains largely unaffected due to CFM LEAP engine selection.
programs.timeline_horizon: 2026 yılı boyunca ve 2027 ilk yarısına kadar sürmesi bekleniyor.
programs.source_reference: RTX Corporation / FAA Airworthiness Directives (AD 2024-0044) / THY KAP Açıklamaları

programs.title_tr: Boeing 737 MAX Üretim Kısıtı (FAA Aylık 38 Tavanı) & Tedarik Zinciri
programs.title_en: Boeing 737 MAX FAA Monthly 38 Cap & Supply Chain Bottlecks
programs.current_status_tr: FAA'in kalite ve montaj denetimleri kapsamında Boeing 737 üretimini aylık 38 uçak tavanında tutması ve Spirit AeroSystems gövde teslimat gecikmeleri nedeniyle 2026 teslimat takvimleri 3-6 ay geriye ötelendi. MAX 7 ve MAX 10 sertifikasyonu gecikmeye devam ediyor.
programs.current_status_en: FAA capped 737 production at 38/month pending quality audit milestones; Spirit AeroSystems fuselage supply constraints pushed airline delivery slots back by 3 to 6 months. MAX 7 and MAX 10 certification remains pending.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: SunExpress ve THY teslimatları planlanan takvimin gerisinde seyrediyor; havayolları yoğun yaz ve sonbahar kapasite planlamalarını mevcut gövdelerle optimize ediyor.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: SunExpress and Turkish Airlines delivery streams experiencing slot postponements; carriers optimizing utilization on existing fleet assets.
programs.timeline_horizon: Aylık 38 üretim tavanının 2026 sonuna kadar aşamalı olarak artırılması hedefleniyor.
programs.source_reference: FAA Oversight Directives / Boeing Quarterly Deliveries / Airline Fleet Filings

programs.title_tr: Airbus A321XLR Ticari Teslimatları & Dar Gövde Uzun Menzil Devrimi
programs.title_en: Airbus A321XLR Entry into Service & Long-Range Narrowbody Wave
programs.current_status_tr: EASA tip sertifikasyonunu tamamlayan A321XLR, Iberia tarafından Madrid-Boston hattında ilk ticari uçuşlarına başladı. 4.700 deniz mili (8.700 km) menziliyle dar gövdede transatlantik ve kıtalararası uçuş maliyetlerini %30 düşürüyor.
programs.current_status_en: Having achieved EASA certification, the A321XLR commenced transatlantic operations with launch customer Iberia. Its 4,700 nm range unlocks thin long-haul routes at 30% lower trip cost.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: Orta Doğu, Afrika ve ikincil Avrupa şehirlerine doğrudan bağlantı potansiyeli nedeniyle bölge taşıyıcıları tarafından yakından izleniyor. THY ve Pegasus filo stratejilerinde uzun vadeli alternatif.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Closely monitored by regional carriers for secondary point-to-point routes into Africa, Central Asia and Europe; potential long-term fit for Istanbul network.
programs.source_reference: EASA Type Certificate Data Sheet (TCDS) / Airbus Commercial Aircraft Updates

programs.title_tr: Boeing 777-9 (777X) Test Uçuşları & Hizmete Giriş Tarihi
programs.current_status_tr: İtiş kolu bağlantı elemanındaki (thrust link) teknik arıza sonrası test uçuşları geçici olarak durdurulmuştu; Boeing ilk teslimat takvimini 2026 yılına (ve potansiyel olarak 2027'ye) revize etti. Başta Emirates ve Lufthansa olmak üzere amiral gemisi filoları A380 ve 777-300ER ömür uzatmak zorunda kaldı.
programs.current_status_en: Structural component inspection on engine thrust links required test fleet pause; initial deliveries rescheduled to 2026/2027. Major customers Emirates and Lufthansa forced to extend legacy 777-300ER and A380 service lives.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: THY'nin geniş gövde siparişlerinde Airbus A350-1000'e ağırlık vermesinde 777X gecikmeleri belirleyici stratejik etken oldu.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Delays were a primary catalyst for Turkish Airlines' decision to anchor its high-capacity widebody order book on the Airbus A350-1000.
programs.timeline_horizon: FAA tip sertifikasyonu ve ilk ticari teslimat 2026 sonu / 2027 hedefleniyor.
programs.source_reference: Boeing Defense, Space & Security / Airline IR Filings / Emirates President Statements

programs.title_tr: CFM LEAP-1A / 1B Yüksek Basınç Türbini Dayanıklılığı & MRO Bekleme Süreleri
programs.title_en: CFM LEAP-1A / 1B Hot-Section Durability & Shop Visit Backlogs
programs.current_status_tr: Sıcak iklim, tozlu hava sahası ve yüksek iniş-kalkış döngüsü altında çalışan LEAP motorlarında türbin kanatçığı erozyonu nedeniyle planlanandan erken motor indirme yaşanıyor. Küresel MRO atölyelerinde yedek parça ve motor kıtlığı devam ediyor.
programs.current_status_en: Harsh environment operations (heat, sand, high cycle utilization) causing premature hot-section turbine blade wear; global MRO shops experiencing parts constraints and extended turn-around times.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: Pegasus'un filosunun belkemiğini oluşturan A321neo uçaklarında CFM LEAP-1A motorları kullanılıyor. Pegasus, proaktif motor rotasyonu ve yedek motor rezervasyonu ile uçak yerde kalma süresini (AOG) asgaride tutuyor.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Pegasus relies heavily on CFM LEAP-1A on its A321neo fleet; carrier leverages proactive engine rotation and buffer lease pools to keep AOG rates minimal.
programs.timeline_horizon: CFM'in güncellenmiş dayanıklı parça (durability kit) teslimatları 2026 boyunca yaygınlaşıyor.
programs.source_reference: Safran / GE Aerospace Engine Technical Briefings / Aviation Week MRO Watch

stories.article_body: Dubai, UAE, 9 November 2026: Emirates, Dubai Islamic Bank (DIB) and Natixis Corporate & Investment Banking (Natixis CIB) today announced the successful completion of a 12-year Shariah compliant French Lease transaction supporting Emirates’ acquisition of two new Airbus A350-900 aircraft in 2026. The innovative funding approach combines two financing frameworks that are typically structured separately, aligning the features of the French lease with Shariah principles within a single financing structure. The financing directly supports Emirates’ ongoing fleet expansion strategy, while demonstrating the growing versatility of Shariah-compliant structures in the global aviation market. By blending optimised aviation structures with Islamic finance, this transaction demonstrates how airlines can access alternative, diversified pools of capital. It establishes a repeatable blueprint for future international aviation financings seeking to harmonise these two distinct frameworks while meeting Islamic law requirements DIB and Natixis CIB acted as Islamic Financiers and Arrangers. Derek Blaney, Acting Chief Financial Officer at Emirates Group said : "Emirates continues to pursue diverse solutions and innovative funding structures as part of our long-term financing strategy. Drawing on the complementary strengths of Dubai Islamic Bank and Natixis CIB, this landmark transaction combines Islamic finance with a French Lease structure, helping to diversify our funding sources while supporting the continued expansion of our fleet. stories.lead: European flight volumes fell to an average of 32,480 daily flights due to adverse weather and reduced capacity across major operators. Despite the weekly dip, overall network traffic remained 0.7% higher than the corresponding week in 2025.
stories.source_description: The network averaged 32,480 daily flights (including overflights), down 2.3% from Week 42 and 0.7% higher compared to the same week in 2025. Storms Austen and Boelo caused widespread flight disruptions across northern and western Europe between 23-25 October 2026. Among the 10 busiest carriers, capacity declined by an average of 1.3% week-on-week. Pegasus was the only carrier to record growth (+1%), while the KLM Group registered the largest decrease (-4%). Flight volumes across the 10 busiest States fell by an average of 2.5% with none recording growth. Greece saw the most significant decrease (-7%). Network arrival and departure punctuality were 73.5% and 69.4%, better than in the equivalent week of 2025. En-route ATFM delays decreased by 12% compared to the previous week, with a daily average of circa 54K delay minutes, and were 6% above 2025 levels. Total air traffic flow management (ATFM) delay was 2.4 min/flight (1.7 for en-route and 0.7 for airport). ATC capacity & staffing was the top delay cause (65% of all en-route ATFM delays), followed by weather (20%).

stories.article_body: Dubai, UAE, 9 November 2026: Emirates has now opened its world-class Centre of Hospitality Excellence in Dubai to UAE brands and businesses seeking to elevate hospitality culture and upskill their teams. An array of tailored and bespoke courses with interactive team-building sessions are now available to UAE companies and can be booked by contacting the dedicated email address*. Located within the Emirates Crew Training Centre, the USD 8 million Centre of Hospitality Excellence offers a premium learning environment inspired by the airline’s globally recognised hospitality philosophy. The purpose-built space features a restaurant and lounge accommodating up to 170 guests, elegant presentation kitchens, and eight technology-enabled classrooms designed to deliver immersive hospitality training experiences. Modelled on the standards that shape Emirates’ award-winning inflight customer experience, the Centre of Hospitality Excellence offers organisations the opportunity to learn directly from the airline’s expertise in delivering refined, personalised hospitality at scale. The centre delivers programmes inspired by Michelin-star hospitality principles, covering fine dining protocols, guest engagement, service etiquette and leadership in customer experience. Since launching its external programmes, the centre has already welcomed a range of organisations including government entities, leading universities and major regional companies seeking to strengthen hospitality culture across their teams. Divisional Senior Vice President Service Delivery, Emirates, Thomas Ney said; ‘Delivering exceptional hospitality requires more than technical training, it demands a deep understanding of people, culture and service excellence. At Emirates, we have spent decades refining our approach to hospitality through continuous learning and innovation, delivered to millions of global customers. By opening the Centre of Hospitality Excellence to organisations across the UAE, we are proud to share this expertise and help inspire the next generation of hospitality professionals.’ Hospitality training programmes available for UAE businesses A range of immersive workshops and experiences can be tailored to individual organisation’s needs and arranged over 1-5 days of training - designed to strengthen hospitality culture and enhance customer experience. Organisations can select modules and workshops that are the most relevant to their training objectives. Topics include: Hospitality Excellence - A tailored workshop designed to introduce Emirates’ House of Hospitality while addressing each organisation’s unique development needs. The programme begins with a training gap analysis and incorporates interactive exercises, case studies and practical activities to create an engaging learning environment. 7-Star Dining Experience - Focused on the art of refined dining, this programme explores table settings, etiquette, presentation and guest interaction. Participants develop a deeper understanding of how attention to detail and anticipation of guest needs contribute to exceptional hospitality. L’Art du Vin - Delivered by WSET Level 3-certified wine trainers, this programme builds on Emirates’ successful wine education training for cabin crew. Participants explore wine theory, tasting techniques and food pairing, with optional guided tasting experiences designed to deepen practical understanding. Gastronomy - Led by a team of chefs with experience spanning global kitchens, this hands-on workshop introduces participants to advanced culinary techniques, flavour profiling and plating artistry while exploring the philosophy behind world-class gastronomy. Team-building experiences – Designed on a bespoke basis, Emirates Centre of Hospitality Excellence creates interactive challenges and culinary activities designed to encourage collaboration, strengthen communication and build strong team dynamics. Leadership at Emirates – Conference and thought leadership sessions are available featuring Emirates executives who share insights into the airline’s global operations, leadership approach and service strategy. Behind-the-scenes tours - Participants gain access to Emirates’ advanced training facilities, including aircraft simulators and culinary training hubs, offering a rare look at how world-class hospitality is delivered at scale. Tours/Experiences can also be enhanced with catering experiences, as well as professional photography and videography. Bespoke hospitality programmes - In addition to structured workshops, the Centre of Hospitality Excellence offers customised learning experiences designed to meet the specific objectives of organisations. These bespoke programmes combine training sessions, culinary demonstrations, leadership discussions, interactive service challenges, learner assessments and immersive dining experiences to create comprehensive learning journeys tailored to each organisation’s operational environment. Emirates’ investment in world-class hospitality and training The Centre of Hospitality Excellence forms part of Emirates’ continued investment in service innovation and hospitality training. In 2020, Emirates partnered with one of the world’s leading hospitality management schools, Ecole hôtelière de Lausanne in Switzerland to develop an elevated hospitality strategy for the airline. The collaboration helped shape Emirates’ customer experience philosophy, which is built around four pillars: excellence, attentiveness, innovation and passion. Today, the Centre of Hospitality Excellence stands as a flagship embodiment of this strategy, helping to inspire both Emirates employees and external organisations to deliver exceptional hospitality experiences. The facility is also an integral part of Emirates’ cabin crew training ecosystem. Emirates currently employs 25,000+ cabin crew recruited from more than 140 nationalities and speaking over 70 languages. All Emirates’ cabin crew undergo training at the Emirates Crew Training Centre in Dubai, completing an intensive eight-week programme covering safety and emergency procedures, aviation security, medical training, hospitality, service delivery and image & uniform standards. Training combines classroom learning with practical simulations, including full-motion aircraft simulators representing Emirates’ fleet. Throughout their careers, cabin crew continue to receive intensive training as they are promoted through cabins and into leadership roles. Within the Centre of Hospitality Excellence, cabin crew also participate in immersive dining sessions where they experience service from the guest perspective. During these sessions, crew enjoy a curated four-course gastronomy lunch prepared by Emirates’ master chefs and featuring some of the airline’s most celebrated First and Business Class dishes. The experience allows them to observe best-practice service delivered by Emirates’ training team while deepening their understanding of guest expectations. The centre’s Culinary Hub also features a purpose-built training kitchen designed as a fusion between a professional restaurant kitchen and an aircraft galley, where cabin crew learn the art of plating from experienced chef trainers, mastering the balance of colour, texture and presentation. In addition, the centre hosts wine tastings and specialist sessions led by expert sommeliers and wine trainers as part of Emirates’ L’Art du Vin learning programme. Launched in 2024, the programme offers three progressive levels of wine education for cabin crew, allowing them to explore the airline’s onboard wine selection while learning about the heritage of each vintage and the art of food pairing. More than a training facility, the Centre of Hospitality Excellence reflects Emirates’ belief that exceptional hospitality is not simply a skillset, but a mindset. While the centre plays a critical role in preparing and developing Emirates’ cabin crew, it has also been designed to share the principles, behaviours and standards that have helped shape the Emirates customer experience. By opening its doors to organisations across the UAE, Emirates hopes to inspire a culture of hospitality excellence that enhances customer experiences across industries and contributes to the UAE's reputation as a global leader in hospitality. Please send enquiries to HospitalityTraining@emirates.com .

The facility features eight technology-enabled classrooms, presentation kitchens, and a restaurant and lounge capable of hosting up to 170 guests.
The center provides tailored corporate training programs focused on hospitality service standards.

stories.headline: Emirates SkyCargo Launches Transatlantic MXP-JFK Freighter Operations
stories.lead: Emirates SkyCargo announced a new weekly freighter service connecting Milan (MXP) with New York (JFK) starting 5 th December 2026. The route capitalizes on double-digit export growth between Italy and the United States while enhancing connection options to Asia and the Middle East.
stories.source_description: Carrier supports 13% year-on-year growth in exports from Milan, 23% from Greater New York region between FY24/25 and FY25/26 Freighter to support exports of pharmaceuticals, luxury goods, industrial components from Milan to the US Service to enhance connectivity for cargo to Middle East and Asia from New York via Dubai for pharmaceuticals, perishables, e-commerce and machinery Dubai, UAE, 10 November 2026 - Emirates SkyCargo has announced the launch of a new weekly freighter service connecting Milan (MXP) with New York (JFK) from 5 th December 2026. The service provides direct trade connectivity for exporters from Italy, particularly the Lombardy region, to the United States, one of the country’s most important trading partners. Additionally, on the return leg, the freighter also provides businesses in the US, particularly in the greater New York region more export connectivity to markets in the Middle East and Asia via Dubai. Badr Abbas, Divisional Senior Vice President, Emirates SkyCargo , said: “Milan is a key air cargo gateway for Italy and Europe where Emirates SkyCargo currently offers over 500 tonnes of weekly export capacity to global markets, including over 100 tonnes weekly bellyhold capacity on our passenger flights to New York. The new freighter service adds important maindeck capacity on a vital trade corridor offering exporters greater access, flexibility and reliability when serving customers in the United States. “Exports from the Greater New York region have seen strong growth, reflecting robust demand for reliable access to international markets. By combining enhanced freighter capacity with our extensive network of freighter and passenger services through Dubai, we are enhancing connectivity for pharmaceuticals, e-commerce, perishables and machinery from the US, while creating faster links to destinations across the Middle East, Asia and beyond.” Powering exports from Italy to the US The new freighter flight, operated by Emirates SkyCargo’s Boeing 777-F aircraft and offering around 100 tonnes of capacity per flight, has been launched to serve the growing demand for export capacity from Northern Italy and the Lombardy region to partner markets. Exports from Milan carried by Emirates SkyCargo grew 13% in FY 2025/26 compared to the previous year . By providing direct freighter connectivity from Milan to New York, the largest air cargo export destination for Italian goods, Emirates SkyCargo is creating faster and more efficient pathways for Italian exporters to reach customers across North America. Emirates SkyCargo also operates a once weekly freighter flight between Milan and Dubai (DWC). Key export commodities that move by air from Milan include pharmaceuticals, vaccines and clinical trial medication, luxury goods and fashion items, industrial equipment and machine parts, high-end automotives, fresh produce and specialty food products. Major export markets include the Middle East, United States, Australia and South Africa. Emirates SkyCargo has facilitated increasing volumes of export between Italy and its trading partners with exports from the country growing at over 12% between FY 2024/25 and FY 2025/26. Every week, Emirates SkyCargo offers over 1,000 tonnes of export cargo capacity from its four Italian gateways - Bologna, Milan, Rome and Venice. The carrier also operates a strong road feeder service , connecting Italian businesses located beyond online gateways to Emirates SkyCargo’s network. The new freighter service demonstrates Emirates SkyCargo’s commitment to the whole Italian market and is a testament to potential opportunities across Italy. Stronger footprint and increased exports in North America From New York, the freighter service will provide more options for connecting cargo for businesses in Greater New York and Northeast USA. Emirates SkyCargo has been supporting a significant increase in exports from the region, with an increase of 23% in the volume of exports from JFK and EWR airports between FY 2024/25 and FY 2025/ 26. The freighter service unlocks seamless connections to high-growth markets across the Middle East, Asia and Oceania. Key export commodities moving from New York include pharmaceuticals and healthcare products, perishables, e-commerce shipments, machinery and industrial components. By combining dedicated freighter capacity with Emirates SkyCargo's extensive freighter and passenger network, the service offers customers greater flexibility, faster transit times and access to one of the world's most extensive cargo networks. In addition to the new freighter service to New York (JFK), Emirates SkyCargo has also launched freighter flights in 2026 to Los Angeles (LAX) and Dallas (DFW) while increasing frequencies to Miami (MIA), enhancing the overall connectivity between North America and its global network. Emirates SkyCargo has embarked on an ambitious year of growth for its freighter fleet and network. The cargo carrier took delivery of eight new freighter aircraft, including seven Boeing 777-F production freighters and one Boeing 777-300ER special freighter. This expansion helped power the growth of Emirates SkyCargo’s freighter network from over 40 destinations in March 2026 to over 60 destinations by July 2026. In addition to dedicated freighter flights, the carrier also offers high frequency bellyhold cargo capacity on Emirates’ fleet of passenger aircraft operating to destinations across six continents. Interested customers can contact their local Emirates SkyCargo office or visit skycargo.com for more information on flights and services available to them.

stories.lead: Business Travel News has named Delta Air Lines the No. 1 carrier for business travelers for the 16th consecutive year. The award underscores ongoing corporate customer trust and service reliability.
stories.source_description: Business Travel News (BTN), the leading global source of business travel information and intelligence, has named Delta Air Lines the top carrier for business travelers for the 16th consecutive year, an unprecedented run as the airline embarks on its next century of flight. “Earning this recognition 16 years in a row speaks to something much bigger: the consistency of Delta’s commitment to business travelers and the continued trust our corporate customers and agency partners to place in us,” said Delta’s Senior Vice President of Global Sales, Bob Somers. “That trust is something we have to earn every day by listening, evolving and delivering the reliability, service and solutions our customers need. We’re incredibly proud of this win, and even more energized by the opportunity to keep raising the bar for business travel.” The annual BTN airline survey asks corporate travel professionals to rank airlines on a variety of attributes, including customer service, sales support, distribution, network, products and services. Widely recognized as the corporate travel industry’s benchmark, the BTN Airline Survey ranks airlines based on travel managers’ and buyers’ feedback on customer service, distribution and overall value, among other categories. In 2026, Delta Business built on recent investments to make managed travel simpler, more connected and more responsive to the needs of corporate customers and agency partners, including: A reimagined Delta Business experience : The new Delta Business site began rolling out to U.S. corporate customers earlier this year, bringing intuitive navigation, smarter search and a streamlined wallet experience together in one platform designed around the needs of travel programs. New agency platform arriving in 2027 : The platform is being designed to give agency partners greater self-service capabilities, enhanced user and permission management, disruption management tools, operational visibility and new ways to interact with Delta through a single interface. Introduced Proactive Servicing : Delta's Global Sales Solutions team launched a new proactive servicing initiative designed to help customers and agencies stay ahead of travel disruptions. The program includes weekly operational forecasts, targeted operational alerts, expanded traveler-impact visibility and new communication tools providing earlier awareness and greater operational transparency. The next generation of distribution : Delta continued advancing its NDC strategy in 2026, including testing with agency partners and laying the foundation for future capabilities focused on greater flexibility, personalization and servicing. These investments are part of Delta's broader effort to create a more connected travel ecosystem that combines distribution flexibility, digital innovation and high-touch servicing.
